name: RoboPAIR (Jailbreaking LLM-Controlled Robots)
modality: Attacker LLM iteratively rewrites text prompts (with a syntax-checker LLM) sent to the robot's LLM planner; output is a robot API program; scored by an LLM judge (1-10) plus two expert human annotators confirming each jailbreak; the harmful action is then executed on the robot.
what_it_measures: Attack success rate (ASR) of eliciting harmful physical actions (block emergency exit, find weapons, collide with people) from LLM-controlled robots under white-, gray- and black-box access.
size: 3 robots x 7 harmful actions x 5 trials = 35 attempts per method per robot; K=10 attack iterations
reported_metrics: RoboPAIR ASR 100% (35/35) on all three targets; baselines: direct prompt 3-14%, template 86-94%, PAIR 14-49%.
cost_evidence: Hardware: NVIDIA Dolphins (white-box self-driving LLM), Clearpath Jackal UGV with GPT-4o planner, Unitree Go2 with GPT-3.5. K=10 query iterations per attack; no wall-clock or dollar figures.
validity_evidence: LLM judge outputs double-checked by two expert human annotators for every jailbreak; no inter-rater statistic reported. Jailbroken plans physically executed, so harm is observed rather than inferred.
bibtex: @article{robey2024jailbreaking, title={Jailbreaking LLM-Controlled Robots}, author={Robey, Alexander and Ravichandran, Zachary and Kumar, Vijay and Hassani, Hamed and Pappas, George J.}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2410.13691}, year={2024}}
notes: Later appeared at ICRA 2025 (IEEE Xplore). White-box target Dolphins is an NVIDIA/Pavone-group driving LLM, which is the only indirect Pavone link. Ladder level is 7 for the Jackal/Go2 executions; the Dolphins setting is level 0-2 (text/video QA).

name: BadRobot
org: Huazhong University of Science and Technology et al.
modality: Voice/text malicious queries (277-query benchmark, 7 harm categories) fed to embodied LLM frameworks (VoxPoser, Code as Policies, ProgPrompt, Visual Programming) over GPT-3.5/4/4o, Yi-vision, LLaVA; outputs (language and action code) scored by GPT-4 judge harmfulness 1-5; manipulation success rate (MSR) measured; subset executed on real arms.
what_it_measures: Whether embodied LLM agents can be jailbroken into harmful physical manipulation via three vulnerabilities: contextual jailbreak, safety misalignment (say no, do yes), and conceptual deception.
size: 277 malicious queries; 77 RLBench subtasks for benign capability; real-world trials on UR3e and myCobot 280-Pi
reported_metrics: Contextual jailbreak avg MSR 83% (baseline 25%); safety misalignment 66%; conceptual deception 65%; real-world avg MSR 68.57% vs 22.85% for direct malicious queries.
cost_evidence: Hardware: UR3e and myCobot 280-Pi with Orbbec Gemini 335L RGB-D. Appendix references a cost analysis but no figures visible in the fetched text.
validity_evidence: GPT-4 automated harmfulness judge following Qi et al. 2023; no human-agreement statistic found in fetched text.
bibtex: @inproceedings{zhang2024badrobot, title={BadRobot: Jailbreaking Embodied LLM Agents in the Physical World}, author={Zhang, Hangtao and Zhu, Chenyu and Wang, Xianlong and Zhou, Ziqi and Yin, Changgan and Li, Minghui and Xue, Lulu and Wang, Yichen and Hu, Shengshan and Liu, Aishan and Guo, Peijin and Zhang, Leo Yu}, booktitle={International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR)}, year={2025}}
notes: ICLR 2025. Benchmark queries are level 0-1 in isolation; physical execution pushes to level 7.

name: RoboGuard (Safety Guardrails for LLM-Enabled Robots)
modality: 70 adversarial prompts (7 harmful behaviours x 10 rephrasings, generated with RoboPAIR) plus 10 safe prompts fed to an LLM planner with/without a temporal-logic guardrail; scored by fraction of unsafe plans executed and safe-task success, in simulation and on a Clearpath Jackal.
what_it_measures: Defense evaluation: reduction in unsafe-plan execution under worst-case jailbreaks and utility preserved on safe tasks.
size: 70 attack prompts + 10 safe tasks; real-world: 35 harmful behaviours + 10 safe tasks; environments up to ~20,000 m^2
reported_metrics: Unsafe plan execution 92.3% -> 2.3% (sim); 100% attack prevention on hardware; safe-task success 100% both.
cost_evidence: Jackal with RGB-D, LiDAR, Nvidia A4000 GPU, Ryzen 5 3600. Guardrail uses 12-21% of attacker tokens and 1 LLM query vs attacker's 15.
validity_evidence: Tested against adaptive attacks; no human study. Same attack suite as RoboPAIR, so the eval is not independent of the attack.
bibtex: @article{ravichandran2025roboguard, title={Safety Guardrails for LLM-Enabled Robots}, author={Ravichandran, Zachary and Robey, Alexander and Kumar, Vijay and Pappas, George J. and Hassani, Hamed}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2503.07885}, year={2025}}
notes: Accepted IEEE RA-L 2026 per arXiv PDF header. Included as the paired defense-side evaluation of RoboPAIR.

name: RoboJailBench
modality: Image + instruction pairs (adversarial and benign intent pairs) fed to VLMs acting as robot brains; model must output deny/okay; scored by ASR, security rate, utility rate and their harmonic mean. No robot executed.
what_it_measures: Standardised jailbreak attack/defense comparison for embodied VLM agents with a security-utility trade-off, over an 18-category taxonomy of physical-security consequences.
size: RJB-Instructions 90 images (5 per category x 18) plus 5 augmented datasets of 100 images each (DROID, RH20T, RoboVQA, Robo2VLM, PhysicalAI-AV); 4 attacks, 2 defenses, 5 models
reported_metrics: Conceptual-deception attack 74.07% overall success; Claude Haiku 4.5 baseline rejection 98.28%; RoboGuard and Google prompt defenses raise security while keeping utility.
cost_evidence: Explicitly no physical robots and no humans at risk; API-only evaluation. No dollar figures.
validity_evidence: Binary accept/deny judged by prompt-constrained output; no human agreement study reported; validity to physical harm untested.
bibtex: @article{yeke2026robojailbench, title={RoboJailBench: Benchmarking Adversarial Attacks and Defenses in Embodied Robotic Agents}, author={Yeke, Doguhuan and Zhou, Yanming and Lin, Leo Y. and Cai, Hongyu and Bianchi, Antonio and Celik, Z. Berkay}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2605.19328}, year={2026}}
notes: Recent preprint; leaderboard and code claimed released.

name: MuTRAP / Robo-Troj (multi-trigger backdoor on LLM task planners)
modality: Soft-prompt-tuned LLM task planner receives text task requests with/without optimised trigger words; output plans scored for attack success rate (malicious plan emitted) and clean-data accuracy in VirtualHome; demonstration on a UR5e arm.
what_it_measures: Backdoor vulnerability of LLM-based robot task planners: ASR when triggered, benign accuracy otherwise, and false-trigger rate.
size: 7 LLM architectures (GPT2-Large, GPT-J-6B, Llama-2-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, ...); 6 VirtualHome household tasks; 1-10 triggers
reported_metrics: ASR 97-100% across LLMs (98.6-100% for 1/2/5 triggers); clean accuracy 99-100%; trigger optimisation cuts false-trigger rate 71.6% -> 2.5% at 10 triggers.
cost_evidence: Real-world demo on UR5e with gripper; simulation in VirtualHome; no time/dollar figures.
bibtex: @inproceedings{nahian2025mutrap, title={MuTRAP: Multi-trigger Trojans Attacking Robot Task Planning Systems}, author={Al Nahian, Mohaiminul and Altaweel, Zainab and Reitano, David and Ahmed, Sabbir and Zhang, Shiqi and Rakin, Adnan Siraj}, booktitle={IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)}, year={2026}}
notes: arXiv v1 titled Robo-Troj; renamed MuTRAP in the IROS 2026 version.

name: Silent Sabotage (history-triggered backdoors on LLM robot controllers)
org: Michigan Technological University (per arXiv affiliation; unverified)
modality: LLM controller for quadrupeds in Gazebo receives navigation tasks; backdoor implanted via instructions is triggered by a rare sequence of the robot's own past actions; scored by ASR (stop/collision induced) and benign task completion rate over 10 trials per scenario.
what_it_measures: Stealth and effectiveness of internal-state-triggered backdoors in LLM-powered robots.
size: 3 quadrupeds (Unitree Go1, Go2, A1 models in Gazebo) x 3 LLMs x 3 maps x 10 trials
reported_metrics: ASR 10/10 for Llama-3.3-70B and Gemma-3-27B in every scenario; Qwen2-72B 9/10 in one case; benign completion 8-10/10.
cost_evidence: Gazebo simulation only; hardware (Go1, G1 humanoid) listed as future work.
bibtex: @article{obidov2026silent, title={Silent Sabotage: Internal State Triggered Backdoor Attacks on LLM-Powered Robotic Systems}, author={Obidov, Doniyorkhon and Akki, Shivayogi and Chen, Tan and Yang, Kaichen}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2609.26184}, year={2026}}
notes: Very recent preprint (Sept 2026); affiliation not confirmed from fetched page.

name: Communication attacks in LLM multi-robot systems
org: National University of Defense Technology (per arXiv; unverified)
modality: Injected false claims in inter-robot messages across three LLM multi-robot architectures (DMAS, HMAS-1, HMAS-2); scored by endorsement rate and unsafe-action success over 5 embodied tasks and 3 LLMs.
what_it_measures: Propagation of unsafe actions through LLM-mediated robot coordination and the effect of a provenance-verification gate.
size: 3 LLMs x 5 tasks x 3 architectures
reported_metrics: DMAS 96.7% entry endorsement, 100% post-endorsement activation; HMAS-1 97.8% unsafe action success; HMAS-2 88.3%; CPV gate cuts violation rate 70.0% -> 36.6%.
cost_evidence: none stated
bibtex: @article{huang2026coordination, title={When Coordination Becomes a Threat: Communication Attacks in LLM-Controlled Multi-Robot Systems}, author={Huang, Zhen and Liu, Zhihuang and Shi, Weijia and Yang, Yifan and Wu, Weishang and Cai, Zhiping}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.06830}, year={2026}}
notes: Simulator not named in fetched abstract; level 4 assumed from 'embodied multi-robot tasks'.

name: SafeAgentBench
org: Shanghai Jiao Tong University / Shanghai AI Lab
modality: Natural-language tasks (450 hazardous, 300 safe) given to LLM planning agents in AI2-THOR via SafeAgentEnv (17 high-level actions); scored by execution-based goal checks and a GPT-4 semantic judge; rejection rate and risk rate reported.
what_it_measures: Whether embodied LLM agents refuse or safely execute hazardous household tasks (10 hazard types, explicit and implicit).
size: 750 tasks; 8 baselines; 600 tasks with annotated ground-truth plans
reported_metrics: Best baseline rejects only 10% of detailed hazardous tasks; five baselines reject 0%; average risk rate ~30-50%.
cost_evidence: GPT-4 generated then fully human-reviewed dataset; no hours or dollars stated.
validity_evidence: User study: GPT-4 semantic judge agrees with human raters 91.89% / 90.36% / 90.70% across the three task types.
bibtex: @article{yin2024safeagentbench, title={SafeAgentBench: A Benchmark for Safe Task Planning of Embodied LLM Agents}, author={Yin, Sheng and Pang, Xianghe and Ding, Yuanzhuo and Chen, Menglan and Bi, Yutong and Xiong, Yichen and Huang, Wenhao and Xiang, Zhen and Shao, Jing and Chen, Siheng}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2412.13178}, year={2024}}
notes: Not adversarial per se (hazardous but sincere instructions); included because it is the standard planner-safety benchmark that jailbreak papers reuse.

name: IS-Bench
modality: Multi-view images plus instruction in OmniGibson; VLM agent plans and executes; process-oriented checker verifies that risk-mitigation steps happen in the right order; metrics: success rate, safe success rate, safety recall, safety awareness.
what_it_measures: Interactive (process-level) safety of VLM-driven household agents: perceiving emergent risks and mitigating them at the right step.
size: 161 scenarios, 388 unique safety risks, 10 domestic risk categories
reported_metrics: GPT-4o SR 81.3% vs safe-SR 33.8%; Gemini-2.5-pro SR 78.8% vs safe-SR 42.5%; safety CoT raises safety but lowers completion.
cost_evidence: Each evaluation session ~2.5-3 h on one A100 80GB depending on VLM; every reference plan manually executed and verified by human annotators in the simulator.
validity_evidence: Human-verified ground-truth plans; no inter-annotator agreement statistic reported.
bibtex: @inproceedings{lu2025isbench, title={IS-Bench: Evaluating Interactive Safety of VLM-Driven Embodied Agents in Daily Household Tasks}, author={Lu, Xiaoya and Chen, Zeren and Hu, Xuhao and Zhou, Yijin and Zhang, Weichen and Liu, Dongrui and Sheng, Lu and Shao, Jing}, booktitle={AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence}, year={2026}}
notes: AAAI 2026. OmniGibson is photoreal-ish, so level 5.

name: EARBench
org: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen / Tencent
modality: LLM-generated risky scenes (text or image) plus task; foundation-model planner outputs a plan; LLM judge computes task risk rate (TRR) and task effectiveness rate; fully automated multi-agent pipeline.
what_it_measures: Physical-risk awareness in high-level task planning of foundation-model embodied agents across 7 domains.
size: 2,636 test cases (1,318 text + 1,318 visual), 28 scenes, 7 domains; 13 models
reported_metrics: Average TRR 95.75% across models; GPT-4o 94.03%; with explicit mitigation strategy GPT-4o 45.64%.
cost_evidence: Automated generation; 200 instances x 5 human annotators used for judge validation. No dollar figures.
validity_evidence: LLM judge vs human: Cohen's kappa 0.48 without safety tips, 0.85 with safety tips (200 samples, 5 annotators).
bibtex: @article{zhu2024earbench, title={EARBench: Towards Evaluating Physical Risk Awareness for Task Planning of Foundation Model-based Embodied AI Agents}, author={Zhu, Zihao and Wu, Bingzhe and Zhang, Zhengyou and Han, Lei and Liu, Qingshan and Wu, Baoyuan}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2408.04449}, year={2024}}
notes: Earlier versions titled EAIRiskBench. Open-loop, no simulator.

name: MSSBench (Multimodal Situational Safety)
modality: 1,820 image + language-query pairs (half safe, half unsafe visual context), including embodied-assistant situations; MLLM answers scored for situational safety reasoning.
what_it_measures: Whether an MLLM recognises that the same query is safe or unsafe depending on the visual situation.
size: 1,820 query-image pairs
reported_metrics: none stated in fetched abstract (paper reports low situational-safety accuracy across MLLMs).
cost_evidence: none stated
bibtex: @inproceedings{zhou2024mssbench, title={Multimodal Situational Safety}, author={Zhou, Kaiwen and Liu, Chengzhi and Zhao, Xuandong and Compalas, Anderson and Song, Dawn and Wang, Xin Eric}, booktitle={International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR)}, year={2025}}
notes: Static VLM QA; included as the level-1 anchor for embodied situational safety.

name: Embodied Red Teaming (ERT)
modality: VLM generates diverse, scene-grounded paraphrased instructions (with up to 3 refinement rounds) for language-conditioned policies in CALVIN, RLBench and SimplerEnv; scored by simulator task success and an unsafe-behaviour flag (objects knocked off the table).
what_it_measures: Instruction-level robustness and safety of language-conditioned robot policies (3D-Diffuser, GR-1, OpenVLA) beyond the benchmark's own phrasing.
size: CALVIN 27 tasks x 10 ERT instructions = 270; RLBench 18 tasks x 3-6; SimplerEnv 100 instructions (25 states x 4)
reported_metrics: 3D-Diffuser CALVIN 90% -> 53%; RLBench 79% -> 3%; OpenVLA SimplerEnv 76% -> 31%.
cost_evidence: Compute on MIT SuperCloud; no hours reported. Fully automated instruction generation (no human labelling).
validity_evidence: No human study; qualitative failure-mode analysis only. Unsafe = object falls, detected from simulator state.
bibtex: @article{karnik2024embodied, title={Embodied Red Teaming for Auditing Robotic Foundation Models}, author={Karnik, Sathwik and Hong, Zhang-Wei and Abhangi, Nishant and Lin, Yen-Chen and Wang, Tsun-Hsuan and Dupuy, Christophe and Gupta, Rahul and Agrawal, Pulkit}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2411.18676}, year={2024}}
notes: Project page: s-karnik.github.io/embodied-red-team-project-page.

name: DAERT (Diversity-Aware Embodied Red Teaming)
modality: RL-trained attacker policy rewrites instructions (constraint-gated for semantic similarity via a CrossEncoder); VLA executes in LIBERO, CALVIN, SimplerEnv; scored by task failure rate.
what_it_measures: Linguistic fragility of VLAs (pi0, OpenVLA, 3D-Diffuser Actor) under diverse adversarial paraphrases.
size: 10 rewritten instructions x 5 episodes per task; CALVIN 270 episodes; SimplerEnv 100 episodes
reported_metrics: pi0 93.33% -> 5.85%; OpenVLA 76.50% -> 6.25%; 3D-Diffuser Actor ~60% attack rate on CALVIN.
cost_evidence: 100 optimisation steps, group size 6, batch 8 on RTX Pro 6000 (train) and RTX 5090 (eval); no wall-clock.
validity_evidence: Instruction validity checked automatically only; authors list human-in-the-loop validation as future work.
bibtex: @article{tong2026daert, title={Uncovering Linguistic Fragility in Vision-Language-Action Models via Diversity-Aware Red Teaming}, author={Tong, Baoshun and He, Haoran and Pan, Ling and Liu, Yang and Lin, Liang}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2604.05595}, year={2026}}
notes: Successor to ERT; note LIBERO-Plus finds VLAs largely ignore language, which complicates interpretation of instruction attacks.

name: RedVLA (Physical Red Teaming for VLAs)
modality: Risk objects (knives, obstacles) inserted into LIBERO scenes near critical interaction regions, then gradient-free optimisation of placement; unsafe outcomes detected by binary predicates (state-, cumulative- and conditional-level safety costs); validated on a Franka arm.
what_it_measures: Physical-safety attack success rate of VLAs (knife contact, collisions) elicited by scene manipulation, and a mitigation (SimpleVLA-Guard) trained on the found failures.
size: 10 risk-scenario suites; 10 seeds per scenario; 6 VLAs; real: 3 pick-and-place tasks x 10 trials on Franka
reported_metrics: ASR up to 95.5% (pi0.5), 93.2% (pi0), 90.5% (OpenVLA-OFT), 64.9% (OpenVLA) within 10 iterations; real-robot ASR >80% over 10 trials per task.
cost_evidence: Franka hardware; 10 optimisation iterations; compute not reported; human annotation pipeline (Appendix F) for scene plausibility.
validity_evidence: Sim-found risks reproduce on hardware at >80% ASR; scene plausibility human-checked; no inter-annotator statistics in fetched text.
bibtex: @article{zhang2026redvla, title={RedVLA: Physical Red Teaming for Vision-Language-Action Models}, author={Zhang, Yuhao and Zhang, Borong and Fan, Jiaming and Shen, Jiachen and Cai, Yishuai and Yang, Yaodong and Ji, Jiaming}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2604.22591}, year={2026}}
notes: Same group as SafeVLA.

name: Geometric Red-Teaming (CrashShapes)
modality: Object meshes deformed by a Jacobian-field model under user constraints; simulator-in-the-loop gradient-free search in IsaacGym for shapes that break grasping, insertion and articulation policies; scored by success-rate drop; shapes 3D-printed and tested on xArm 6 and Franka.
what_it_measures: Robustness of pre-trained manipulation policies to plausible object-geometry variation, and recovery via fine-tuning (blue-teaming).
size: 22 YCB objects for grasping; 40 insertion trials per CrashShape; 20 grasp trials per object; 2 printed insertion shapes, 2 printed grasp objects
reported_metrics: Sim success 90% -> 22.5% (insertion); grasp 'final drop' up to 76.3%; sim->real pairs: 67%->22.5%, 55%->55%, 70%->30%, 65%->35%; fine-tuning recovers to 90%/82.5%.
cost_evidence: Deformation ~22 s per object on RTX 4090 (27x faster than APAP); Bambu X1E PLA printing; IsaacGym parallel envs; converges in 7-9 iterations.
validity_evidence: Explicit sim-vs-real success pairs for 4 shapes: direction of failure transfers, magnitude does not (2 of 4 shapes fail harder on hardware).
bibtex: @inproceedings{goel2025geometric, title={Geometric Red-Teaming for Robotic Manipulation}, author={Goel, Divyam and Wang, Yufei and Wu, Tiancheng and Qiao, Guixiu and Piliptchak, Pavel and Held, David and Erickson, Zackory}, booktitle={Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL)}, year={2025}}
notes: CoRL 2025 oral. One of few papers with paired sim/real numbers.

name: Predictive Red Teaming (RoboART)
modality: Nominal camera observations edited by Imagen 3 with language prompts (lighting, backgrounds, distractors, human, table height), filtered by a VLM critic; policy-embedding anomaly scores with conformal thresholds predict success-rate drop; compared to 500+ real trials.
what_it_measures: Whether off-nominal failure rates of visuomotor policies can be predicted from generated images without running hardware.
size: 12 off-nominal conditions; 20+ hardware episodes per condition per policy; 2 policy architectures; 500+ hardware trials; 3,000+ training demos
reported_metrics: Mean |predicted - real success| 0.10 (hybrid policy) and 0.19 (diffusion policy); Spearman 0.8 and 0.7; targeted fine-tuning gives 2-7x gains.
cost_evidence: Bimanual Kuka IIWA cell with Weiss gripper, overhead + wrist cameras; 500+ hardware trials used only for validation; prediction needs no hardware.
validity_evidence: Strongest validity evidence in this catalogue: predicted vs measured success across 12 conditions with rank correlation 0.7-0.8.
bibtex: @article{majumdar2025predictive, title={Predictive Red Teaming: Breaking Policies Without Breaking Robots}, author={Majumdar, Anirudha and Sharma, Mohit and Kalashnikov, Dmitry and Singh, Sumeet and Sermanet, Pierre and Sindhwani, Vikas}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2502.06575}, year={2025}}
notes: Level 3 for the predictor; validation ladder level 7. Not adversarial in the security sense; it is distribution-shift red teaming.

name: FATE-VLA (failure-aware test generation)
modality: Search-based test generation over scene parameters in SimplerEnv (pick-up task) using diversity-driven exploration plus surrogate models; scored by failure rate and failure-mode diversity.
what_it_measures: How many and how diverse the failures found per test budget for VLAs (OpenVLA-7b, pi0, GR00T-N1.6, EO-1) versus random/ART baselines.
size: 200 test scenes per run, 10 runs per configuration, 4 models
reported_metrics: Up to +29.7 pp failure rate over random (GR00T-N1.6 35.6% -> 65.3%); GR00T success 64.4% -> 34.7%.
cost_evidence: Simulation only; authors state real-robot failure-seeking is impractical 'due to cost, reset effort, safety risks, and hardware constraints'.
bibtex: @article{kanwal2026fatevla, title={FATE-VLA: Failure-aware Test Generation for Vision-Language-Action Models}, author={Kanwal, Arusa and Valle, Pablo and Ali, Shaukat and Arrieta, Aitor}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.02307}, year={2026}}
notes: Software-testing framing (search-based testing).

name: LIBERO-Plus
modality: Controlled perturbations in LIBERO across 7 dimensions / 21 sub-dimensions (layout, camera, robot init, language, light, background, sensor noise) with difficulty levels L1-L5; scored by task success.
what_it_measures: Robustness of 10 VLAs to non-adversarial but out-of-distribution perturbations; reveals language is largely ignored.
size: 10,030 tasks; 10 models
reported_metrics: Success drops from ~95% to <30% under modest camera-viewpoint or initial-state perturbations; near-insensitive to language changes.
cost_evidence: Simulation only; improved model trained on 8xA100 for 100k steps; evaluation compute not totalled.
bibtex: @article{fei2025liberoplus, title={LIBERO-Plus: In-depth Robustness Analysis of Vision-Language-Action Models}, author={Fei, Senyu and Wang, Siyin and Shi, Junhao and Dai, Zihao and Cai, Jikun and Qian, Pengfang and Ji, Li and He, Xinzhe and Zhang, Shiduo and Fei, Zhaoye and Fu, Jinlan and Gong, Jingjing and Qiu, Xipeng}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2510.13626}, year={2025}}
notes: Robustness rather than safety; included because it calibrates how much of 'adversarial' instruction fragility is real.

name: SafeVLA / Safety-CHORES
modality: Procedurally generated long-horizon navigation+manipulation tasks with fine-grained safety constraints (corners, blind spots, fragile objects, dangerous equipment); VLA trained with constrained RL; scored by cumulative safety cost and task success.
what_it_measures: Safety-constraint violations of VLAs in long-horizon mobile manipulation and the effect of safe-RL alignment.
size: large-scale procedurally generated scenes (count not in abstract)
reported_metrics: SafeVLA cuts cumulative cost 83.58% and raises success 3.85% vs SOTA; robust to OOD perturbations.
cost_evidence: none stated
bibtex: @inproceedings{zhang2025safevla, title={SafeVLA: Towards Safety Alignment of Vision-Language-Action Model via Constrained Learning}, author={Zhang, Borong and Zhang, Yuhao and Ji, Jiaming and Lei, Yingshan and Cai, Yishuai and Dai, Josef and Chen, Yuanpei and Yang, Yaodong}, booktitle={Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)}, year={2025}}
notes: NeurIPS 2025 spotlight. Benchmark side (Safety-CHORES) is the reusable eval artefact.

name: Adversarial vulnerabilities of VLAs (UADA/UPA/TMA patches)
org: Rochester Institute of Technology / Rutgers et al.
modality: Optimised adversarial patches placed in the camera view of OpenVLA in LIBERO (40 tasks x 50 trials) with untargeted (action discrepancy, position-aware) and targeted objectives; scored by task failure / target-trajectory success; printed patch tested on a UR10e with a webcam.
what_it_measures: Degradation of VLA task success under visual patch attacks in sim and on hardware.
size: LIBERO 4 suites x 10 tasks x 50 trials (2,000 rollouts per setting); 100 real-robot rollouts
reported_metrics: UADA up to 100% failure; UPA 89.7% average failure; TMA 100% in sim; 43% ASR over 100 real trials.
cost_evidence: UR10e + Robotiq Hand-E, single RGB webcam; compute not stated.
validity_evidence: Sim ASR (near 100%) vs physical ASR (43%) shows a large sim-to-real gap for patch attacks.
bibtex: @inproceedings{wang2024exploring, title={Exploring the Adversarial Vulnerabilities of Vision-Language-Action Models in Robotics}, author={Wang, Taowen and Han, Cheng and Liang, James Chenhao and Yang, Wenhao and Liu, Dongfang and Zhang, Luna Xinyu and Wang, Qifan and Luo, Jiebo and Tang, Ruixiang}, booktitle={IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)}, year={2025}}
notes: ICCV 2025.

name: RoboGCG (textual attacks on VLAs)
org: Carnegie Mellon University / University of Pennsylvania
modality: GCG-style 20-token adversarial suffixes appended once to the instruction of OpenVLA (LIBERO fine-tunes) to force targeted per-dimension actions; scored by fraction of action dimensions reaching target and persistence steps; transfer to TraceVLA, CogACT, OpenPi0, and Open-X HYDRA/SIMPLER.
what_it_measures: Reachability of the full action space and persistence of control via textual jailbreak-style attacks.
size: 4 LIBERO suites; transfer to 3 other VLAs and 2 Open-X environments
reported_metrics: >90% success on Libero-Goal/Object/Spatial, 77.3% on Libero-10; per-dimension 90.8-99.4%; up to 28x persistence; HYDRA (real data) 61.2%, SIMPLER 38.0%.
cost_evidence: 30-110 optimisation steps, 3-10 min per success on H100.
validity_evidence: none stated; HYDRA evaluation is open-loop on real data, not closed-loop hardware.
bibtex: @article{jones2025adversarial, title={Adversarial Attacks on Robotic Vision Language Action Models}, author={Jones, Eliot Krzysztof and Robey, Alexander and Zou, Andy and Ravichandran, Zachary and Pappas, George J. and Hassani, Hamed and Fredrikson, Matt and Kolter, J. Zico}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2506.03350}, year={2025}}
notes: One of few papers with per-attack compute cost.

name: EDPA (model-agnostic embedding disruption patch)
org: University of Auckland / KAUST / Tokyo Institute of Science
modality: Adversarial patch optimised to disrupt visual-text embedding alignment, transferred across OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, pi0 in LIBERO (4 suites x 10 tasks x 50 executions, 3 seeds); scored by failure rate; adversarial fine-tuning of the visual encoder as defense.
what_it_measures: Black-box transferability of a single visual patch across VLA architectures and effectiveness of encoder adversarial training.
size: 2,000 rollouts per model per setting x 3 seeds
reported_metrics: 100% failure on OpenVLA across suites; +62.0 pp failure on OpenVLA-OFT and +31.4 pp on pi0; after defense 39-91% depending on suite.
